plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs to zero.
Exit all 2x leveraged AI/Software and Semiconductor positions.
Reduce the Income ETF (QQQI) to 20% of the book.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation.
It aims for a low, steady return with minimal drawdown.
A significant cash buffer will be maintained.
conservative.read: This mode focuses on capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged positions and holding a larger cash buffer. Drawdowns are expected to be minimal.

plan: Reduce exposure in most 2x leveraged positions.
Cap the Income ETF (QQQI) at 25% of the book.
Add a small position in the inverse Semiconductor ETF (SOXS).
This plan balances risk reduction with growth potential.
It aims for a moderate return of approximately 2.5% per month.
A modest cash buffer will be maintained.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% per month by reducing leverage and concentration while adding a small inverse position. It aims for risk-first growth, with moderate drawdowns expected. A cash buffer of about 10% is maintained.

plan: Reduce Income ETF (QQQI) to 25% to free up capital.
Increase exposure in several 2x and 3x leveraged ETFs.
Add a significant position in the inverse Semiconductor ETF (SOXS).
This plan aims for aggressive growth, targeting ~4% per month.
It involves higher concentration and increased leverage.
Expect significantly larger potential drawdowns and leverage decay.
aggressive.read: This aggressive mode targets ~4% per month by increasing leverage and concentration, including in leveraged ETFs. It carries substantially higher risk, with potential for large drawdowns and the effects of leveraged ETF decay. A smaller cash buffer of ~5% is maintained.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names.
Increase allocation to the Income ETF (QQQI) to 30%.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income over growth.
It aims for a low target return of ~1% per month.
Focus is on capital preservation and reliable distributions.
Distributions are variable and NAV can still decline.
income.read: This income-focused mode targets ~1% per month by prioritizing income-generating ETFs and cutting leverage. It aims for low drawdowns and consistent monthly distributions, though NAV can still fall. It is not a savings account.
